statement: The function returns a result r and: if there exist integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b < len(nums) and sum_{i=a}^{b} nums[i] >= k, then r = min{ b-a+1 | 0 <= a <= b < len(nums) and sum_{i=a}^{b} nums[i] >= k }; otherwise r = -1. Here the sum is the ordinary integer sum of the entries, and a subarray is non-empty and contiguous.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (no arithmetic overflow, no out-of-bounds access, and no panic).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 1 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, there exist integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b < len(nums), b-a+1 = r, and sum_{i=a}^{b} nums[i] >= k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r for (nums, k), if r != -1, then for every integer k' with 1 <= k' <= k, the set { b-a+1 | 0 <= a <= b < len(nums) and sum_{i=a}^{b} nums[i] >= k' } is nonempty and its minimum is at most r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.

statement: Let nums' be the sequence of length len(nums)+m+n0 such that nums'[i] = 0 for 0 <= i < m, nums'[m+i] = nums[i] for 0 <= i < len(nums), and nums'[m+len(nums)+j] = 0 for 0 <= j < n0. Whenever the function returns a result r for (nums, k), if there exist integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b < len(nums') and sum_{i=a}^{b} nums'[i] >= k, then r = min{ b-a+1 | 0 <= a <= b < len(nums') and sum_{i=a}^{b} nums'[i] >= k }; otherwise r = -1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000; m and n0 are non-negative integers with len(nums)+m+n0 <= 100000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] > 0, and sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] < k, then r = -1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if r = len(nums), then sum_{i=0}^{len(nums)-1} nums[i] >= k.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -100000 <= nums[i] <= 100000; 1 <= k <= 1000000000.
